newsitem.title: USA: Jewish leaders to meet in Oslo on Swiss issue.
newsitem.headline: Jewish leaders to meet in Oslo on Swiss issue.

text.p: About 150 Jewish leaders will meet in Oslo next week to decide whether to expand to other European countries their campaign against Switzerland for the return of "lost" Jewish bank accounts.

The meetings of the World Jewish Congress on next Monday and Tuesday were planned to take place just as a joint Jewish-Swiss committee was to begin the unprecedented task of sending audit teams to search secret Swiss bank records to find out how much money deposited by Jews before and during the Second World War was returned to its rightful owners.

Swiss bankers and politicians, embarrassed by allegations that their country profited from the Holocaust, were considering whether to create a fund for victims of Nazism in a gesture of reconciliation.
Swiss financiers and politicians said a fund was one option for responding to months of Jewish-led attacks on the Swiss financial role in the war.

A previously secret 1942 U.S. Justice Department document released on Wednesday accused Switzerland of being "economically under Axis domination no matter what the sentiments of the people" and said all Swiss imports and exports had to have German or Italian approval.
The document, found in the U.S. National Archive by WJC researchers, also accused Swiss banks of being used by the Nazis to invest German money in the United States and Latin America during the war.

A WJC spokesman said the group's president, Edgar Bronfman, will give the Jewish leaders at next week's Oslo meeting a briefing on the success of restitution efforts so far, ask for policy decisions on how to further pursue claims against Swiss banks and discuss whether to expand the campaign to other European countries.

Meanwhile, British M.P. Greville Janner, a WJC vice president, was expected to tell delegates that Britain, France and the United States agreed to delay distribution of six tons of looted Nazi gold until the claims of Holocaust victims were considered.

The gold, held in the Bank of England and in the Federal Reserve Bank in New York, was to have been distributed to national banks in Europe. But Janner was expected to report the distribution has been delayed "until all other options have been considered."
The six tons were believed to be the last looted Nazi gold in Allied hands.
Norwegian Prime Minister Thorbjorn Jagland will address the group on Norwegian restitution efforts to compensate his country's Jews for the property taken from them by the wartime Quisling regime.
